comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C6-C9. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the data showing PDF-1 pathway regulation of daf-7 specifically in ASJ neurons of males to be convincing and well-supported by Figure 1B-C.

Agreement on claims C17-C22. Both evaluations accept the data showing PDF-1 pathway mutants have normal pathogen responses. Peer reviewer requests additional male behavioral data for completeness but does not dispute the hermaphrodite findings.

Strong disagreement on claims C25-C31. OpenEval finds the cell-autonomous action strongly supported by multiple approaches (rescue, RNAi, Cre-lox). Peer Reviewer #2 finds this 'not so convincing,' arguing overexpression could be artifactual and requesting cell-specific RNAi in ASJ as stronger necessity evidence.

Agreement on concerns about claims C47-C51. Both evaluations find the FISH data problematic. OpenEval notes qualitative nature and inconsistency (only 20% males show puncta despite robust functional requirement). Peer reviewers request proper quantification, better controls, and clearer demonstration of ASJ overlap.

Disagreement on claims C41-C45 (and C76). OpenEval finds the gain-of-function experiments in hermaphrodites strongly support that PDFR-1 activity is limiting for sex-specific daf-7 expression. Peer Reviewer #2 argues this could be overexpression artifact and notes inconsistency with prior masculinization experiments, suggesting cell non-autonomous regulation instead.

Disagreement on claims C12-C15. OpenEval finds the epistasis analysis coherent and well-supported with appropriate logic for parallel pathways. Peer Reviewer #2 questions whether the data fully demonstrate PDF regulation of mate searching through daf-7 in ASJ, requesting reciprocal rescue experiments with cell-specific expression.

Partial overlap on claims C34-C35. OpenEval finds the data appropriately support ACY-1 acting downstream of PDFR-1. Peer Reviewer #1 finds the acy-1(gf) data 'intriguing' but raises concerns about pathway placement and requests additional clarification experiments to establish the hierarchy.

Partial overlap on claims C37-C38. OpenEval finds the starvation data appropriately place nutritional state downstream/parallel to cAMP signaling. Peer Reviewer #1 accepts the starvation data but requests additional experiments (acy-1 loss-of-function tests) to clarify the regulatory hierarchy.
OpenEval finds claims C57-C60 (summary conclusions) well-supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these summary claims.

OpenEval finds claims C73-C79 (mechanistic model) coherent and well-supported, with appropriate qualifications for speculative aspects. No direct peer review evaluation of these model claims, though R6 indirectly challenges the PDFR-1 sex-specific expression model (C76).
OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C4, C10, C11, C16 as appropriately supported by citations. Peer reviewers do not evaluate background/contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C5, C23, C24, C32, C33, C39, C40, C52-C56 as appropriately supported by prior literature. Peer reviewers do not evaluate these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C61-C72 as appropriately supported by citations establishing broader significance. Peer reviewers do not evaluate these contextual claims.
